indicators.note: tailless says the final letter of the word for kind is cut off

parts.note: a sort is a kind or type

explanation.surface: Someone inspecting a herd of donkeys, apparently a stubby-tailed breed.
explanation.definitionFit: An assessor is an official who evaluates or inspects, for instance property values or exam work.

clue.text: Appear so excited about old TV show

indicators.note: about means around, so the jumbled letters go round the abbreviation for old
excited means stirred up, so the letters of appear so are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone seems thrilled about a television programme from years ago.
explanation.definitionFit: A soap opera is a long-running serial drama on television, named for the soap makers who sponsored early ones.

clue.text: Surrey town in memo spelt the wrong way

indicators.note: the wrong way says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A town name written backwards by mistake in an office note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' marks the letters concealed in 'memo spelt', and 'the wrong way' reads them backwards. Surrey is a county south-west of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Epsom is a town in Surrey famous for its racecourse, home of the Derby.

indicators.note: disrupted means thrown into disorder, so the letters of remains are rearranged

explanation.surface: A class whose survivors have had their session interrupted.
explanation.definitionFit: A seminar is a small class where students meet with a tutor to discuss a subject.

clue.text: Goalkeeper's cap in red for game

indicators.note: in says that letter goes inside the word for red

parts.note: ruby is a deep red colour

indicators.note: a cap sits on top, so the first letter of goalkeeper's is taken

explanation.surface: A goalie's headgear coloured red for the match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goalkeeper' and 'cap' suggest football, but the sport is the oval-ball game.
explanation.definitionFit: Rugby is a team sport played with an oval ball, an example of a game.

definitions.meaning: to run is to rush or sprint
a small amount, as in a splash of milk

explanation.definitionFit: To dash is to run quickly, and a dash is also a small quantity added, such as a drop of brandy.

clue.text: Requiring change, stand up for rubbish collector

indicators.note: requiring change means needing to be altered, so the letters of stand up are rearranged

explanation.surface: A demand to rise up and do something about the binmen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rubbish collector' suggests a binman, but it is the small shovel that gathers sweepings.
explanation.definitionFit: A dustpan is the flat scoop into which dirt and crumbs are swept from a floor.

indicators.note: emptying removes the contents, leaving only the outside letters of stop

explanation.surface: An instruction not to drain the tub.
explanation.definitionFit: A spa is a mineral spring or a place for therapeutic bathing; Bath itself is a famous English spa town.

indicators.note: something in a muddle is jumbled up, so the letters of also are rearranged

explanation.surface: A nation that is likewise in disarray.
explanation.definitionFit: Laos is a landlocked nation in Southeast Asia, bordering Vietnam and Thailand.

clue.text: A-lister seen principally in Margate, surprisingly

indicators.note: surprisingly signals that the letters turn up in an unexpected order
principally means chiefly, at the head, so the first letter of seen is taken

explanation.surface: A celebrity spotted, against all expectations, in the seaside town of Margate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surprisingly' shuffles S plus MARGATE. Margate is an English seaside resort in Kent, not a likely haunt of celebrities.
explanation.definitionFit: An A-lister is a top-tier celebrity, which is exactly what a huge star is.

clue.text: Greedy type has quite a few, hosting a New Year celebration

parts.note: a hog is a greedy person who takes more than a fair share

indicators.note: hosting means holding a guest within, so the word for quite a few has the a placed inside it

explanation.surface: A glutton invites plenty of guests to a party for the turn of the year.
explanation.definitionFit: Hogmanay is the Scottish name for New Year's Eve and its festivities.

clue.text: Choose something a miner would select?

definitions.meaning: a miner's tool, the pointed implement used to break rock

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading puns on 'select': a miner would pick out this digging tool, a pickaxe.
explanation.definitionFit: To pick is to select, and a pick is also the pointed tool miners use to break up rock.

indicators.note: necking means swallowing, so the jumbled letters go inside the word for idiot

parts.note: a clown is a fool or idiot

indicators.note: incorrect means wrong, so the letters of dose are put in the wrong order

explanation.surface: Someone foolish has swallowed the wrong amount of medicine and must be halted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'necking' is British slang for gulping down a drink, here taking the letters in.
explanation.definitionFit: To close down is to stop operating, as when a business or broadcast shuts.

clue.text: Ludicrously complex Briton, he has moved on

indicators.note: moved means shifted around, so the letters of these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A British man has relocated and gone on his way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moved' looks like the Briton relocating but is the anagram signal. W. Heath Robinson was a British cartoonist famous for drawing absurdly elaborate contraptions.
explanation.definitionFit: The cartoonist's name became an adjective for any gadget that is absurdly over-engineered for a simple task.

parts.note: to tally is to agree or match

explanation.surface: Absolutely, it has to be a perfect fit.
explanation.definitionFit: Totally is a synonym meaning completely or entirely.

definitions.meaning: a large crusty bread loaf with diagonal slashes on top
a blunder, something made by mistake

explanation.definitionFit: A bloomer is a British loaf with a slashed crust, and in British slang also a silly mistake.

clue.text: Huge supply initially put in tank

indicators.note: put in says that first letter goes inside the word for tank

parts.note: a vat is a large tank for liquids

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so the first letter of supply is taken

explanation.surface: Instructions for filling a large container with a delivery.
explanation.definitionFit: Vast is a synonym meaning immense or enormous in size.

indicators.note: a renovation rebuilds something, so the letters of costlier are reassembled

explanation.surface: A refurbishment that costs more than planned, carried out on a religious house.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is by example, hence 'say?': a cloister is a covered walkway in a monastery and, by extension, a monastery or convent itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A cloister can mean a religious house where monks or nuns live secluded, so a monastery is one instance.

definitions.meaning: to go across or over, as with a road

explanation.definitionFit: To cross is to pass over something, and the cross is the chief emblem of the Christian faith.

parts.note: a peak is the top of a mountain

explanation.surface: Someone is about to state what came second-best.
explanation.definitionFit: To say something is to utter it, a synonym of talking.

clue.text: Dance venue clearer, everyone going in

indicators.note: going in says the word for everyone is placed inside the word for clearer

parts.note: a broom clears a floor by sweeping

explanation.surface: At a dance venue, the sweeper clears out while the crowd arrives.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballroom is a large hall built for formal dancing.

indicators.note: into says the town lies within the run of letters across sunday racing

explanation.surface: A Scottish town that goes in for horse racing on the Sabbath.
explanation.definitionFit: Ayr is a coastal town in south-west Scotland, known for its racecourse.

indicators.note: back says the word for hurt is read from end to start

explanation.surface: A deity has injured his back.
explanation.definitionFit: Eros is the Greek deity of love, counterpart of the Roman Cupid.

indicators.note: welcoming means taking someone in, so a goes inside the word for cook

parts.note: to fry is to cook in fat

explanation.surface: A chef who greets guests with a punch-up.
explanation.definitionFit: A fray is a brawl or noisy fight, as in 'enter the fray'.
Striking describes something that catches attention, and it is also the present participle of a verb for landing a blow.
